 Tarantino’s Final Film Is Written, but a West End Swashbuckler Goes First
 Quentin Tarantino says his tenth and final film is already written, but a West End play and time with his family will come before any…
 By Patricia Gorman 
 · October 18, 2026 
 · 3 min read 
 Photo: World of Reel (all rights reserved) 
 Quentin Tarantino has finished the script for what he has long said will be his tenth and final film, Variety reported on October 17. He won't move on it until his stage play closes.
 He made the comments on The Graham Norton Show, his first appearance on the programme in more than a decade. Ellen DeGeneres, Colin Farrell and Gemma Chan were fellow guests.
 What Tarantino said about the script
 Tarantino told Norton he likes the script he has written. First, he wants to do the play and see who he is afterwards. Then he will go home to his family and take some time before deciding what comes next.
 World of Reel's Jordan Ruimy pointed out that this looks like a new project rather than The Movie Critic, which that site described as dead and buried. World of Reel said the premise of the new film is unknown.
 The Popinjay Cavalier on the West End
 The play is called The Popinjay Cavalier and stars Sacha Baron Cohen. It opens at London's Phoenix Theatre next March. Previews begin in late February. The run lasts three months and ends on June 13.
 The idea started life as a screenplay, Tarantino said. Then he realised it worked better on stage. He expects it to be thrilling. According to World of Reel, he described it as springing from the swashbuckling movie genre with a French farce quality.
 When the production was announced, Tarantino said in a statement that he was keen to give the West End a great night out, Variety noted.
 A long gap between films
 His most recent film remains Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, released in 2019. It won Brad Pitt the Oscar for best supporting actor. Tarantino earned nominations for best picture and best director.
 World of Reel noted that the wait since 2019 will reach eight years by next summer. That already exceeds the six-year pause after Jackie Brown, which the site called the longest dormant stretch of his career.
 The site also pointed to the family side of his plans. Tarantino and his wife, Daniella Pick, have two children, with a third on the way. World of Reel guessed that the tenth film would arrive in 2028 at the earliest.
 That would happen only if the play does not persuade him that the stage is where he belongs. The timeline is the site's own estimate, not Tarantino's.
 For now the schedule is simple, with the play opening in March and closing in June. After that, Tarantino said, he will decide what to do with a finished script.
